pages.text: It was a late-summer night. Today they would see fireflies. Grandpa took two flashlights.
Nils really wanted to see the sparkling fireflies. But the night forest was so dark. He gripped his flashlight.
They walked the forest path. Nils shone the light this way and that. Beyond the light, he was too scared to look.
"From here, lights off to see them." Nils shook his head. "Don't turn off the light! It's dark!"
He waved the flashlight around. Wherever it shone, only grass lit up. Not one firefly.
One firefly brushed past Nils. As soon as he shone the light, it vanished.
Night grew deeper. Nils still hadn't had a look at the fireflies, just held his flashlight tight.
Click. Grandpa turned his light off and stood quietly beside Nils.
Click. Nils turned his off too. Dark at first, then little by little he could see. Grandpa held his hand firmly.
Here and there in the grass, fireflies sparkled. Nils lowered the flashlight and opened both eyes wide. Blink, blink, blink.
